{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"A passing loop (UK usage) or passing siding (North America) (also called a crossing loop, crossing place or, colloquially, a hole) is a place on a single line railway or tramway, often located at a station, where trains or trams travelling in opposite directions can pass each other.","title":"Passing loop"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Trains/trams going in the same direction can also overtake, providing that the signalling arrangement allows it.","title":"Passing loop"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" A passing loop is double-ended and connected to the main track at both ends, though a dead end siding known as a refuge siding, which is much less convenient, can be used.","title":"Passing loop"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" A similar arrangement is used on the gauntlet track of cable railways and funiculars, and in passing places on single-track roads.","title":"Passing loop"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"\"No Reason\" is the fourth single and second track by the Canadian rock band Sum 41, from their fourth studio album \"Chuck\" (2004).","title":"No Reason"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It was released in the United States and Europe as a promotional single.","title":"No Reason"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The song is the main track of the soundtrack of the movie \"Dirty Love\".","title":"No Reason"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Before the movie's premiere, Sum 41 released an unofficial music video for the single as a promotion for the movie, showing the band's scene in the movie where they play live, along with various other scenes from the movie.","title":"No Reason"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" It was the band's last single before the departure of Dave Baksh in May 2006.","title":"No Reason"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"Who directed the film that had \"No Reason\" as its main track?"}
